subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw keep this issue as the canonical core `openclaw notify` CLI/Gateway/Control UI contract, fold it into broader notification architecture, or reject shell-originated UI alerts in favor of plugin/external delivery?
rationale: The requested feature is absent and useful, but it creates a new shell-facing admin capability and UI interruption policy that cannot be safely chosen from source inspection alone.

options.title: Design the core notify contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the focused CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC contract before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader notification architecture
options.body: Make the wider Control UI notification tracker own the UI queue/action model, with this issue contributing the shell/admin broadcast requirement.

options.title: Prefer plugin or external delivery
options.body: Reject a core command and document the supported plugin, Web Push, channel, or external-notifier path instead.

recommendation.title: Design the core notify contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the focused CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest history match for the CLI and Gateway broadcast policy surfaces that determine this product/security boundary.
